lexical_decisions.rationale: The Hiphil infinitive construct of נחל with prefixed ב marks a temporal clause, and in context refers to assigning inheritances among nations. 'Gave the nations their inheritance' is idiomatic English that preserves the distributive sense better than a wooden 'caused to inherit.'
A divine title here. English convention normally includes the article in this construction, and 'the Most High' preserves the title's force without paraphrase.

In Deuteronomy this refers to the various peoples/nations of the world, not specifically 'Gentiles' in a later Jewish-Christian contrast. The article is supplied for natural English reference to the class as a whole.
Another temporal infinitive construct with 3ms suffix referring back to the Most High. 'Separated' fits the plain sense of פרד here and pairs well with the following object.

Per the project's gender-accurate policy, the masculine form is retained where the Hebrew is explicitly masculine and representative. 'Sons of man' is a fairly literal rendering of בני אדם and preserves the poetic register. A more inclusive sense is possible, but the source expression is not flattened in the main text.
The Hiphil of יצב conveys setting firmly or establishing. 'Fixed' communicates decisive placement of boundaries in natural English.
'Boundaries' fits territorial delimitation, and 'peoples' avoids repeating 'nations' too closely while still matching עמים as ethnic/political groups.

alternatives: in proportion to the number of
lexical_decisions.rationale: This prepositional phrase indicates correspondence or measure. 'According to the number of' is the most idiomatic and sufficiently formal rendering.

Provisional rendering of the selected published 4Q37 phrase, not an approved source change. ‘Divine beings’ is an interpretive rendering; ‘sons of Israel’ represents the retained Masoretic/Samaritan source alternative, and ‘sons of El’ the separately identified conjecture. These are not interchangeable glosses of one source form. No new lexicon consultation or full-verse manuscript attestation is claimed.

theological_decisions.rationale: This unapproved candidate follows the published Hebrew-based working selection and retains contrary readings in the apparatus. The divine referent does not settle exact earliest Hebrew wording or broader theological interpretation. The candidate is for source/English review only; it does not promote the existing selection or satisfy its pending gates.

The Hebrew is grammatically masculine and representative. In keeping with the project's gender-accurate policy, the main text preserves the masculine form rather than replacing it with a gender-neutral paraphrase, while acknowledging the broader human reference in a footnote.

footnotes.text: 4QDeutj (4Q37) reads ‘sons of God’; the Masoretic Text and Samaritan Pentateuch read ‘sons of Israel.’ The main Greek Septuagint reading is ‘angels of God.’ The earliest exact Hebrew wording remains debated; ‘sons of El’ is an editorial reconstruction rather than an extant Hebrew reading in the consulted sample edition.
'The sons of man' is a Hebrew expression for human beings or humankind.

translation.text: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of man[b], he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God[a].
